ratings_why.fun: Building toward a Full you can aim, then watching Hares turn into copies of your best units, is a real payoff, but five new ideas make every turn a reading exercise.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: a public moon cycle you bend to choose which round you spike is a timing game no tribe today has, and Borrowed shape makes Hares glue that grows other tribes' text.

verdict_why: The Three Hares and Hare in Her Form can't be read as written; fixing their wording is a real improvement, not just a change.

points.text: The Three Hares says "the others of the three", but touching is a whole chain, so the three are never named. Say "this and the two units directly touching it on the zigzag".

Hare in Her Form doesn't say when the bolt fires (Start of Combat if alone, or the moment its last row-mate dies) or whether it can fire twice. The "unless every unit in that row has this text" clause is hard to read; simpler: "If every unit in its row has this, ignore it."
The Moon-Scour's builds rely on it doubling borrowed text, but the card doesn't say so. Add "including borrowed text" so a player knows.

An italic phase in front reads two ways: *Waning* Moonturn means "turns to Waning", *Waxing* End of Turn means "during Waxing". Writing the first as "Moonturn to Waning:" would make Dusk Doe and Meikle Care readable at a glance.

Mother Meikle Care plus The Hare in the Moon overshoots Full to Waning, a trap two strong cards set for each other. The designer's own fix, "Turn the Moon to Full", keeps the charm and removes the trap.

standouts.why: Jill Longshanks boxing again after every win is March boxing you can see, and it reads in one pass.
Leveret in the Form growing only when left alone is the real animal in one line, and it makes a placement choice.
Old Wat boxing their biggest unit, dying and buffing the team is the thrown-out suitor as a card.

weakest.why: Suitor Jack is a generic adjacent buffer; nothing in it says a jack being boxed back across the field.
Spring Jill's text works one fight in four, so most rounds she is a vanilla body.
The Three Hares has the best icon in the seed but the hardest text to read in the tribe.

flags.note: Which units count as "the three" isn't defined.
Bolt timing and repeat are not stated.
With golden Dame Waxwell and golden Mad March Hare it reaches hundreds of stats a turn, as the designer notes.
Copying the enemy across in fight swings from a 5/7 Shield to a copy of a capstone; the fight UI must show what she borrowed.
